items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: we had Sidney Bechet and Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, and he was the only one that received an award at this festival.

ctx.x: have been like that with musicians, that I would share what I have, like I knew how to...well, I won't say I knew how to get money from women, but I knew...well, you know, women liked me and they would want to do me favors, and if some guy...you understand, Dan, wasn't doing too well, he could always come to me. That guy was here, right here. One time I owed my rent...my rent was a thousand dollars and his rent was a hundred and I had a hundred dollars. And you know what I did? I gave it to him. He paid his rent.…

You know, Danny, during those years singers were the principals. You don't think that Coleman Hawkins could take his tenor saxophone player and go out and stand in front of Butter-Beans and Susie and be the star. He was just another musician in the background. Maybe they'd let him play a number. Maybe. Or he'd have an opportunity when they did have an

opportunity to play was when the chorus girls...you know, you could really do your thing and play as hard as you wanted to which would be an inspiration to the chorus girls. But other than that they didn't have, you know, very seldom would you have a band that was the attraction. I can't even remember when they ever did that on the TOBA. And it's quite possible, but I'm telling you from my knowledge what they would do. They would...a guy would come on the show...he could play when the chorus girls were dancing,…
